title: Occam's Razor
coreMove: Choose the simplest sufficient explanation first, then add complexity only when the evidence forces it.
sourcePressure: Frozen support is moderate and narrow through official model reference and table-of-contents identity. Keep to preferring the simpler sufficient explanation or structure, and state clearly that simplicity is not proof.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says the simplest explanation is automatically true or that complexity is always suspicious.

sourceAnchors.name: Occam's razor
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen source supports Occam's razor as a Volume 1 model and authorizes a narrow paraphrase: prefer the simpler sufficient explanation, not simplicity as automatic proof
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Start with the lean explanation that fits the evidence, then let the evidence decide whether it deserves more machinery.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a homeowner and installer diagnosing a sudden solar drop
exampleSpecs.stakes: unneeded panel replacements could cost thousands
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Charlotte checks the tripped inverter breaker before accepting a theory about failing roof panels
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a silent inverter box beside a blinking breaker

exampleSpecs.audience: a claims supervisor reviewing a delayed water-damage file
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fraud theory may delay a legitimate payout
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Steven tests the ordinary explanation, a missing plumber invoice, before building a complex fraud narrative
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp folder with one empty invoice tab

exampleSpecs.audience: an aquarium technician troubleshooting a loud exhibit pump
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may order a new pump when a clogged intake explains enough
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu clears the intake mesh and watches the noise stop before approving the expensive pump replacement
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a low metallic hum vibrating through a wet concrete floor

exampleSpecs.audience: a choir director explaining why altos keep missing rehearsal
exampleSpecs.stakes: the director may blame commitment when a calendar conflict explains enough
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Clara checks the school concert calendar before inventing a morale theory about the alto section
exampleSpecs.firstImage: folded sheet music on an empty row of alto chairs

exampleSpecs.audience: a facilities lead facing complaints that all office printers are unreliable
exampleSpecs.stakes: a vendor replacement could miss the one network queue causing failures
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo compares failure timestamps and tests the single print server queue before replacing hardware
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three jammed printouts cooling beside a server-room badge

exampleSpecs.audience: a park administrator explaining a sudden booking drop
exampleSpecs.stakes: marketing money may be wasted if a broken date filter explains the drop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Kira test one date filter before accepting a broad theory about changing camper preferences
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an empty campsite calendar with one blocked weekend highlighted

skillTargets: know when extra complexity is warranted
test the lean explanation against evidence

tryThisNowSpec: Take one problem and write the leanest explanation that fits all current evidence. Add one evidence item that would force a more complex story.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
